video.title: 3 Tips to Rip the Low Backhand

classification.reason: The coach provides clear, actionable instructions including dipping the back knee deep, hinging at the hips with a straight back to tilt the torso, and shoving the hands forward so they clear the front foot.

problem.title_as_question: How can you rip low backhands effectively?
problem.definition: Recreational players struggle to attack and drive low backhands with pace and spin, often staying too upright and failing to extend forward through contact.

quotes.text: All right, we're going to go over three fundamentals that will help you rip the low backhand.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The first one is this back knee, and I want you to see just how deep that is.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: We need to get this knee deep for balance purposes and so we can use it to drive through the ball.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: you can press through that knee, press that back foot through towards your target, and you'll see Alexa do it here a couple times where she's able to slide that foot forward.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And this knee is out over the toe here. That is the most athletic, most efficient way to play this ball. So, that's the first to dip this back knee.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: A lot of rec players when they hit this shot, they're a lot straighter than they think.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: They might think they're bending the knee, but they are not really sitting down into this deep knee bend position that's necessary to really excel on this ball.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: The second fundamental we're going to talk about is the angle of the torso.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Her back is erect. It's not curved. She's not bent over in the sense that her back is curved, but her hips are hinged, and that allows her racket path to go more low to high than usual.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: When you tilt like this, that makes your hands naturally go low to high with the same biomechanically efficient swing that you always use.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: We also have to tilt the torso, hinge at the hips, back straight. We're not bending over like curling over, but tilt the torso, hinge at the hips.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: That's how you attack these low balls and get the hands to fly up when you throw them out away from your body like you normally do.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: For our third fundamental, we're going to use the side view. This is the same set of backhands. So, we can see just how far out in front of her Alexa's hands are flying.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So, if you look at her front foot there, her hands are clearing her front foot every stroke.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: We don't finish over our shoulder because we're yanking the racket over our shoulder. We throw the racket forward. We drive the racket forward.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: And then by coincidence, it often finishes over the shoulder, but not always.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: So, that's our third thing. Take the hands, shove them forward, forward, forward through the ball. They should clear your front foot on it pretty much every single backhand you hit.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: Yeah, that's good execution there. I probably need to practice this more when I play.
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: The player stays much straighter with insufficient knee bend when attempting to hit low backhands.
The player curls or curves their back instead of hinging cleanly at the hips.
The player yanks the racket up over the shoulder instead of extending forward past the front foot.

causes.statement: The player does not sit into a deep back knee bend, preventing them from maintaining balance and driving through the low ball.
The torso is not tilted forward from a hip hinge with a straight back, preventing the swing path from naturally dropping low-to-high.
The player yanks the racket over the shoulder rather than throwing and driving the hands forward through the shot.

angles.summary: Tilting the torso via a hip hinge allows the player to maintain their standard biomechanically efficient swing while naturally creating a low-to-high path.
Players wrongly yank the racket over the shoulder deliberately on the two-handed backhand, whereas a shoulder finish should only happen naturally after driving forward.
Positioning the back knee deep and out over the toe recruits the quadriceps to drive the body and back foot forward toward the target.

solutions.summary: Dip the back knee deep over the toe and press the back foot forward toward the target as you drive through the ball.
solutions.external_goal: press that back foot through towards your target

solutions.summary: Tilt the torso by hinging at the hips while keeping the back straight rather than curling the spine.
Shove your hands forward, forward, forward through the ball rather than yanking the racket over your shoulder.
solutions.external_goal: shove hands forward through the ball
